subject: Finance signer vs procurement approver — AWS private offer structure for BrightWave
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@brightwave.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@brightwave.com>, AWS Marketplace Seller Support <aws-seller-support@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: signer and approver for private offer (BrightWave)

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the pilot looked great. Procurement at BrightWave is ready to accept a private offer via AWS Marketplace, but there are two internal signers we need to reconcile: our Finance/FP&A lead (who needs to sign the PO for billing authority) and Procurement (who needs to approve terms/contractual language).

To move quickly: can Redwood specify whether the private-offer PDF should list the Finance signer as the official buyer, or should Procurement be listed as the approver and Finance as the payment contact? AWS Marketplace has a single "Buyer" field on PO activation and that may trip our internal routing. If you can share how you typically structure this (or if you can provide a template), we can get Legal/Finance to clear it this week.

Attached is our internal approval matrix (procurement-approval-matrix.xlsx) and a short note from our procurement manager (Daniel). Appreciate a short call if that's faster.

Best,
Sofia Ramirez
Head of Partnerships, BrightWave
sofia.ramirez@brightwave.com

Attachment: procurement-approval-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@brightwave.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: signer and approver for private offer (BrightWave)

Sofia — thanks for the clear note and the matrix. Looping in Vivek and Ben so we have finance and marketplace ops visibility, and Neha on approvals. Quick answers up-front:

- For AWS private offers we usually populate the "Buyer" field with the legal entity that will be billed (Finance signer). Procurement is recorded as the approver/point of contact in the purchase narrative or in the activation notes.
- If BrightWave requires Procurement to be the contractual signee instead of Finance, we can map Procurement as the "Approver" and add a billing contact field that points to Finance — but that increases procurement/legal review time on their side.

Action items:
1) Can BrightWave confirm which legal entity will be billed (full legal name exactly as in their tax docs)?
2) If Procurement must sign, ask for the name/email of the signee and an expected lead time for procurement sign-off.
3) We will attach our standard private-offer PDF template and the minimal routing language we put in the description to avoid activation delays.

I attached the template and our SOC2 evidence pack stub for procurement review. If helpful we can do a 20-min call tomorrow.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Office: +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: BrightWave_AWS_Private_Offer_Draft_v1.pdf (pdf), Evidence-Pack-SOC2-Redwood.zip (zip)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@brightwave.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: signer and approver for private offer (BrightWave)

Adding a couple of operational notes from finance/ops perspective:

- Preferred: list billed entity as Buyer (this keeps activation with AWS consistent and reduces risk of invoice routing errors). The PO will present to Finance as payable; Procurement can be referenced in the notes for contract approval audit trail.
- If BrightWave insists Procurement signs the PDF, we will need Procurement's signature block and a corresponding PO line that maps to the billed entity. That is doable but requires 48-72 hours extra for our legal/finance to review the mapping.
- For term length: annual prepaid vs 12-month consumption are both supported. Annual prepaid with a commitment favorite for co-sell crediting and predictable co-sell metrics. If they want usage-based, we recommend a 12-month billing cadence to stabilize reporting.

I'll also flag that AWS seller support wants the buyer legal name exact match to the AWS account to avoid activation holds. Ben — can you confirm if there are any known activation gotchas when procurement and finance diverge on signer vs payer?

-Vivek

On Fri, Jun 26, 2026 at 08:50 AM PST Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Happy to confirm — primary activation holds we see are: mismatch between buyer legal name and AWS seller console entry, and missing contact emails for activation/tax remittance. If Procurement signs but Finance is billed, include the Finance remittance email and a note in the PO description.
> 
> Also: if BrightWave requests multi-year term >1 year there are additional approval gates on our side (rev recognition and co-sell crediting). For a clean pilot, recommend 12-month term.
> 
> -Ben

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@brightwave.com>
